findings.what: The report-body API remains a second reachable P7-completion path: write_report defaults complete_readme=True, while complete_report_readme verifies only findings/report and not the chart output or chart receipt.
findings.why: PRD.md:218-221 says run_workflow is the only completion-state owner and report APIs write artifacts/receipts only; skills/anomaly/SKILL.md:90-92 says README completion occurs only after every P7 output succeeds. A direct write_report call can still write `Status: complete` and `Last completed phase: P7` before charts exist, and tests/test_review.py:412-421 explicitly preserves that stale behavior. Revise that consumer contract, make write_report body-only, and ensure completion projection fails unless all final outputs—including charts—are present.

findings.what: Proven-unused compatibility surface remains in the durable runner: RetryLimitExceeded plus read_state, read_events, invalidate_downstream, record_invalidation, resume, and execute_phase aliases have no repository consumers.
findings.why: The task's simplicity objective explicitly called for deleting obsolete aliases/dead paths. These names add API surface and maintenance choices without protecting behavior; repository-wide search finds only their declarations.

findings.what: The extraction separates responsibilities but leaves a mutual dependency: workflow.run_workflow lazily imports product_workflow, while product_workflow imports WorkflowRunner, PHASES, and private _completed_phase/_next_phase helpers from workflow.
findings.why: Product policy is now easier to locate, but dependency direction did not become clean and the composition owner depends on runner internals. Make the boundary one-way and expose only the minimum public runner operation rather than private state interpretation.

findings.what: The test suite defines a second 64-line P0-P7 handler composition whose P3/P4 responsibilities differ from the installed product composition; it is used only to seed the invalidation matrix and supply one P1 handler.
findings.why: This is avoidable duplicate policy and much of the test bloat. Seed the matrix through the checked-in public demo and exercise the event-failure case through run_workflow (or one explicit handler), so tests reuse the canonical composition instead of maintaining a parallel one.
